extracted.intended_audience: literate readers interested in manners, wit, and comic performance (early-18th-century Spectator readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for social performance: what makes good dancing, agreeable company, comic/storytelling talent, and sound editorial or public conduct as discussed in Spectator essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dancing as a method to instill good breeding and virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Method like this, to give young Women a Sense of their own Value and Dignity; dancing, properly performed, communicates that value to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good dance performance should display modesty and becoming behaviour, convey a genuine sense of dignity, and be used to cultivate honourable sentiments. Example behaviours: casting a respectful eye, assuming a majesty of aspect that commands respect, smiling modestly to please a parent. Anti-pattern: treating dancing as mere wanton exhibition or as an excuse for immodest behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modesty and becomingness as central qualities in a dancer
rubrics_metrics.description: The most becoming Modesty ... casting a respectful Eye ... the innate Principles of a modest Virgin, a tender Wife, a generous Friend, a kind Mother, and an indulgent Mistress are to be shown in the dancer's countenance and motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate dancers by the modesty and appropriateness of their deportment: a graceful, restrained carriage that suggests virtuous character is preferable to flashy or provocative affectations. The performer's expression and gestures should reinforce social virtues rather than undermine them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cheap physical tricks and animal-like antics
rubrics_metrics.description: The flippant insipidly Gay and wantonly Forward ... fly, hop, caper, tumble, twirl, turn round, and jump over their Heads ... many Animals can do better than a Man, instead of performing to Perfection what the human Figure only is capable of Performing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: valuing ostentatious, acrobatic, or purely attention-seeking feats over refined human motion. Good practice emphasizes movements that suit human grace and expressiveness, not feats that imitate animals or circus tricks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion and change of posture/aspect to enhance personhood
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion, and change of Posture and Aspect, has an Effect no less surprising on the Person ... (illustrated by a portrait with many dresses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use varied posture and expression intentionally to highlight different qualities of the person; subtle changes in motion and countenance can greatly alter perception. Judges should note how movement and aspect affect the overall impression, not just static features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligence/understanding as prerequisite for good dancing
rubrics_metrics.description: No one ever was a good Dancer, that had not a good Understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess dancers not only on physical skill but on taste and judgment. Understanding the art—its proprieties, rhythm, and expressive aims—is essential; mere physical agility without taste is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discernment of defect and the power to reveal the ridiculous
rubrics_metrics.description: He had so exquisite a Discerning of what was defective in any Object before him, that in an Instant he could shew you the ridiculous Side of what would pass for beautiful and just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful wit/comic performer discerns flaws or excesses and makes them visible (often humorously) to an audience. This should be done with skill and proportion so as to amuse and instruct rather than merely to injure. Example: pointing out the ridiculous in things commonly admired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling with natural, unexpected incidents and well-turned repartee
rubrics_metrics.description: He was no less skilful in the Knowledge of Beauty; there is no one who knew him well, but can repeat more well-turned Compliments, as well as smart Repartees ... in his inimitable Faculty of telling a Story, in which he would throw in natural and unexpected Incidents ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good comic storytelling combines felicitous phrasing, repartee, and the insertion of surprising but plausible incidents. Evaluate the teller by variety, timing, and the capacity to alternate praise and raillery to suit the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt audience tone: vary sharpness according to company
rubrics_metrics.description: Then he would vary the Usage he gave them, according as he saw them bear kind or sharp Language. He had the Knack to raise up a pensive Temper, and mortifie an impertinently gay one, with the most agreeable Skill imaginable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comic performer must read the room and adjust severity of satire or teasing accordingly; the same jest should be made gentler or sharper depending on who is present. Successful comic effect depends on this adaptive control to avoid unnecessary offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mimicry should capture manner of thinking as well as outward manner
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Accounts he gave of Persons and Sentiments, he did not only hit the Figure of their Faces, and Manner of their Gestures, but he would in his Narration fall into their very Way of thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective imitation penetrates to the subject's mental habits, not only their gestures or voice. Good mimicry reveals and exaggerates thought-patterns for comic insight; poor mimicry only caricatures surface features and is less illuminating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance entertainment with restraint among refined company
rubrics_metrics.description: He could keep the Discourse to himself the most Part of it, and maintain his good Humour with a Countenance in a Language so delightful, without Offence to any Person or Thing upon Earth, still preserving the Distance his Circumstances obliged him to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful companions know when to perform and when to be reserved: a judicious silence and tempering of humour preserves dignity and prevents offense. Evaluate performers on their ability to be charming without transgressing decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: What makes an admirable social character (Manilius model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberality almost bearing the Name of Profusion; splendid Frugality at home; plain, genteel and unaffected garb; civility and attention to others; a mixture of Gravity enlivened with Wit and Humour; an engaging Softness; mild and gentle, yet vigorous in service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspects to value in judging a person's social worth: generous public behaviour combined with modest private economy; simplicity of dress that does not seek to dazzle; attentive listening; witty but instructive conversation; balance between cheerfulness and seriousness. These traits make a person pleasing and universally admired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities that disqualify a man from public office
rubrics_metrics.description: A Man is unfit for such a Place of Trust, who is of a sower untractable Nature, or has any other Passion that makes him uneasie to those who approach him ... a Dilatory Temper ... and any degree capable of Corruption ... gratifications, tokens of thankfulness, dispatch money are pretences under which Corruption shelters itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For evaluating fitness for office, look for: absence of roughness, pride, impatience; promptness and industry (delay is treated as ongoing injustice); integrity (refusal of gratuities). Prefer candidates with liberal education and virtuous habits; men of learning tend to discharge offices with greater honesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial practice for classical texts: include only meaningful various readings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a different Reading gives us a different Sense, or a new Elegance in an Author, the Editor does very well in taking Notice of it; but when he only entertains us with the several ways of spelling the same Word ... they only take up the Time of the learned Reader, and puzzle the Minds of the Ignorant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should record variants that alter sense, metre, rhyme, or produce new elegance; avoid exhaustive lists of trivial orthographic variants. Consider metre and rhyme, weigh manuscript authority, and avoid burdening readers with inconsequential readings. Example: prefer readings that preserve metre/rhyme or clarify sense over pedantic spelling differences.
